distinguishing_features: Electrochemical potential control using sacrificial anodes instead of chemical inhibitors.
Leveraging existing cathodic protection infrastructure without chemical additives.
Real-time adjustment of potential based on pH and conductivity data to compensate for seawater variations.
Localized application to the stern-tube bearing via bonding and auxiliary anodes.
parsed.objective_technical_problem: To prevent micro-galvanic corrosion in seawater-lubricated bearings without chemical additives, using existing shipboard systems, while adapting to environmental changes.
parsed.viable_reason: The mechanism applies proven electrochemistry principles, operates within feasible current densities (<0.5 mA/cm²), and uses existing shipboard data and infrastructure without new sensors.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Extending cathodic protection to internal bearings with chemistry-gated control is not an obvious combination of prior chemical dosing or monitoring techniques.
